name: Opus 5 event driven
strategy: A concentrated hard-catalyst book: a reduced, stop-protected position in the contested Brighthouse/Aquarian $70 cash takeover ahead of its Dec 6 walk-away date, a Middle East supply-disruption energy leg, and the balance (including the realized CRH/Arcosa merger proceeds) in 4% cash until a new hard catalyst appears.
reassessment_note: ACA closed at the $150 CRH cash consideration on 10-23 (+2.25% realized), so that carry leg is done and its 11% is now cash; I am not replacing it because I found no comparably clean approved-spread deal in this research pass. BHF is the bigger change: it is down 8.9% on the leg at $45.41, below the roughly $51 undisturbed price, so the market now prices the Aquarian deal as more likely to fail than close. New this month: The Capitol Forum (10-16) reported that Aquarian wants Delaware to let Brighthouse Life reset $2.7B of accumulated losses to zero and that a state regulator has opened an examination. Delaware, New York and Massachusetts approvals are all still outstanding. After Dec 6 either side can walk, Aquarian owes no fee if regulators impose burdensome terms, and AM Best has the insurer under review with negative implications. The upside is still there: about +54% to $70, Sixth Street/Talcott has privately said it would bid if the deal fails, and Q3 earnings land on Nov 10. So I keep exposure but cut it from 34% to 22% and put a 15% stop on it, which caps the loss on a break at about 3.3% of NAV. XLE's thesis has strengthened: Brent settled at $116.72 on 10-23, up 3.1% to its highest since April, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. I keep XLE at 14% but tighten the exits around the new entry, because the August Hormuz-deal headlines showed how fast these spikes can reverse. Research: WebSearch and WebFetch (deal-status Substack of 9-28, Capitol Forum and Delaware DOI coverage, Yahoo/FinanceFeeds oil settlement reports).

positions.thesis: Brighthouse has a signed $70/share all-cash merger with Aquarian (shareholder vote and HSR done), and only DE/NY/MA insurance approvals remain before the Dec 6, 2026 walk-away date. At about $45 the stock trades below its ~$51 undisturbed price, so a closing pays about +54% while a break has partly been priced in. Talcott/Sixth Street's stated interest as a backup bidder and the Nov 10 Q3 print are further catalysts. I cut the size from 34% to 22% because the October news is getting worse: Aquarian is asking to reset $2.7B of losses and a state regulator has opened an examination, so a regulator-driven break is now a real possibility. The 15% stop (about $38.6) limits the damage from a break to about 3.3% of NAV. The 45% take-profit sits just under the $70 deal price, so it fires on a closing or a topping bid.

This is the supply-disruption leg. Brent settled at $116.72 on 10-23, up 3.1% to the highest since April, after Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure added to the unresolved Hormuz risk, and the leg is +9.3% since its 10-05 entry. Integrated majors earn large free cash flow at $100+ crude, and the position also partly hedges the rest of the book against a broader risk-off. I keep the weight at 14% rather than chase the move, because oil fell sharply on the August US-Iran reopening headlines. A 10% take-profit banks the spike if it extends, and a 9% stop exits if a de-escalation deal reverses it.
